title: PM-99217-prd-regulated-degradation-playbook-and-verification-harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Translate the KV-cache / coldstart postmortem action items into a concrete PRD addition that defines 'regulated degradation modes' (what the system may do when SLOs are threatened), required observability changes, and an automated verification harness. This ticket scopes the PRD text, acceptance criteria, rollout controls, and the synthetic test suite required for release gating.

Background: Recent incident (incident-2026-02-kv-regen) exposed unclear behavioral contracts when primary model pools degrade: ad-hoc fallbacks caused user-visible latency spikes and token-cost regressions. Postmortem recommended: deterministic fallback contracts, throttle windows, explicit degradation modes, and synthetic verification before rollout. This PRD will ensure product, runtime, and SRE share a single source of truth for allowed behaviors and verification steps.

Primary deliverables: 1) PRD section describing regulated degradation modes (Graceful Throttle, Fallback-Variant, ReadOnly-Cache, Blackhole-Minimise) with exact trigger conditions; 2) A verification harness checklist and synthetic test scenarios (traffic mixes, coldstart bursts, KV-regeneration path) that must pass before canary -> prod; 3) Observability requirements (new metrics, dashboard slices, alert threshold definitions, and a trace-level failure classification) tied to acceptance criteria; 4) Rollout gating rules (canary sizes, automatic rollback triggers, manual approval gates) and required playbook updates.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement runtime code changes; it only specifies requirements, test harness design, and rollout contracts. Implementation tickets will be created for runtime, console, and SRE work.
problem_statement: When underlying pools degrade (KV regeneration, kernel regression, or cold starts), the platform currently lacks a bounded set of allowed behaviors and measurable release gates. This ambiguity leads to inconsistent fallbacks and unpredictable customer impact.
goals: Define 3-5 discrete degradation modes with deterministic triggers and allowed fallback behaviors
Specify synthetic scenarios and pass/fail criteria that cover common incident modes (KV regen, coldstart spike, kernel slowdown)
Add observability requirements (metrics, dashboards, retained traces) mapped to acceptance criteria
Create rollout gating rules and an approval checklist to prevent silent regressions in serving behavior
scope_changes: Add explicit PRD clauses that require runtime teams to expose a small set of boolean signals and rate-limit knobs. Require SRE to maintain a synthetic test runner in CI that can inject degraded signals and validate user-facing latencies and cost per token targets. This expands scope from a documentation-only PRD to a cross-team verification contract. Any runtime implementation beyond telemetry exposure will be scoped into follow-up ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains named degradation modes with exact trigger thresholds and allowed fallback actions for each mode
Synthetic harness defines at least 6 scenarios with pass/fail thresholds and runbook links
Observability spec lists required new metrics (per-route degradation-state, fallback-count, avg-p99-latency-under-degradation) and draft dashboard mockups
Rollout gating rules documented: canary sizes, auto-rollback thresholds, manual approval steps, and notification recipients
Security and compliance review completed for behavior that alters customer request routing
Stakeholder sign-off from Runtime, SRE, Console, and Legal recorded in PRD comments
success_metrics: Reduction in unplanned fallback variance: target 90% reduction in customer-facing latency regressions in post-deployment 30 days
Mean time to detect mis-deployment via synthetic harness: < 5 minutes
No high-severity incidents attributable to ambiguous fallback contracts for 90 days after rollout
rollout_plan: Draft PRD -> internal review (2 business days)
Finalize PRD and attach synthetic scenarios and dashboards (1 day)
Create implementation ENG tickets and verification CI job (parallel) and schedule a canary for next release window
Canary: 1% traffic with synthetic verification running continuously; if any pass/fail threshold breaches, auto-rollback and page on-call
